name: Nurse Practitioner and Advanced Practice Nurse
description: ⚠⚠⚠ Florida grants nurse practitioners autonomous practice — and almost every account of it omits the limit that matters. Autonomous registration covers PRIMARY CARE ONLY. It does not let you practise your specialty without a physician protocol, and only certified midwives are excepted. 11,201 APRNs were registered for autonomous practice as of the 2024 legislative analysis. ⚠⚠ The occupation itself is nearly twice the size of the physician assistant profession — 320,400 employed, 29,500 openings a year, $132,300 median.
credentialNote: ⚠⚠⚠ READ THE SCOPE LIMIT BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE. Section 464.0123, F.S. lets an APRN register for autonomous practice with an unencumbered licence, no discipline in five years, 3,000 clinical practice hours within five years under physician supervision, 3 graduate semester hours each in differential diagnosis and pharmacology, and liability coverage of at least $100,000 per claim. ⚠⚠ But the statute permits autonomous practice ONLY IN PRIMARY CARE — family medicine, general paediatrics and general internal medicine — with no surgical procedures except subcutaneous ones. ⚠⚠⚠ The Florida House staff analysis of HB 771 states it plainly: all APRN specialties are eligible for autonomous practice, HOWEVER only certified midwives are currently authorised to practise any specific functions related to their SPECIALTY area without an established physician protocol. So a psychiatric nurse practitioner who registers as autonomous may run a family practice independently and still needs a protocol to practise psychiatry. ⚠ HB 771 (2024) would have changed that for psychiatric nurses; it DIED in the Healthcare Regulation Subcommittee on 8 March 2024, and the 2025 statute still reads primary care only. ⚠⚠ THE DEGREE: there is no Florida statute requiring a doctorate. NONPF committed in 2018 to move entry-level NP education to the DNP by 2025 and reaffirmed it in 2023, but NONPF is an association of faculties, its commitment carries no regulatory force, and both AANP and ANCC still certify master's-prepared NPs. Only a state board of nursing can set the degree for licensure.
bodyHtml:
⚠⚠⚠ Autonomous practice is primary care only, and that is the whole story

Florida has granted nurse practitioners autonomous practice since 2020, and it is real: 11,201 APRNs were registered for it when the legislature last counted in a 2024 staff analysis. The limit that gets left out of almost every summary is what it covers.

What autonomous registration gives youWhat it does not
✅ independent practice in primary care — family medicine, general paediatrics, general internal medicine⚠⚠ your specialty — a physician protocol is still required for specialty functions
✅ admitting, managing and discharging patients at health care facilities⚠ surgery, beyond subcutaneous procedures
✅ physicians' certifications and signatures, with a statutory exception—

The Florida House staff analysis puts it in one sentence: “All APRN specialties are eligible for autonomous practice, however, only certified midwives are currently authorized to practice any specific functions related to their specialty area without an established physician protocol when registered for autonomous practice.”

⚠⚠⚠ So a psychiatric nurse practitioner who registers as autonomous can independently run a family practice and still needs a protocol to do psychiatry. The same analysis counted 3,458 psychiatric nurses in Florida, of whom 1,093 held primary-care autonomous registration — people holding an independence that does not reach the work they actually do.

⚠ HB 771 (2024) would have fixed exactly that. It died in the Healthcare Regulation Subcommittee on 8 March 2024, and the 2025 statute still reads primary care only. If you read elsewhere that Florida psychiatric NPs practise independently, check the statute rather than the article.

The three advanced practice roles

RoleSOC2025 medianEmployedOpenings/yrFL public programmes
Nurse practitioner29-1171$132,300320,400✅ 29,5008 award the DNP
⚠⚠ Nurse anesthetist29-1151⚠⚠⚠ $236,59053,800⚠ 2,700⚠ 3, awarding 55 a year
Nurse midwife29-1161$134,040⚠ 8,600⚠ 500—

⚠⚠⚠ Nurse anesthesia is the best-paid nursing role in the United States — $104,290 above the nurse practitioner median — and it has 2,700 openings a year nationally against the NP's 29,500, with three Florida public programmes producing 55 graduates. Pay and access run in opposite directions, exactly as they do in nuclear medicine.

⚠ Nurse midwifery is smaller still at 8,600 jobs and about 500 openings — but note it is the one specialty the autonomy statute actually unlocks.

⚠⚠ Against the physician assistant, on the statutes

Nurse practitionerPhysician assistant
Median$132,300$135,880
Employed✅ 320,400162,700
Openings a year✅ 29,50012,000
Independence✅ autonomous in primary care (s. 464.0123)⚠ supervised (s. 458.347)
Scope⚠ primary care for autonomy; specialty needs a protocol✅ every specialty, including surgery
Employer constraintnone once registered⚠ a physician may supervise at most 10
Degree in law⚠ no statutory requirementmaster's required by statute, matriculation after 31 Dec 2020
Getting inRN licence first, then graduate school⚠ ~3,200 hours of patient contact before applying

⚠⚠ The pay is within $3,580 and the structure is completely different. Nurse practitioner is nearly twice the profession by headcount and 2.5 times by annual openings; the PA route buys scope and gives up independence; the NP route buys independence in one setting and gives up the rest of medicine.

⚠ And the way in differs more than the way out. A PA applicant accumulates clinical hours in any job that qualifies. An NP applicant becomes a registered nurse first and gets the hours by being one — which is a longer road but a paid, licensed and self-contained one, and if you stop halfway you are still a nurse.

⚠⚠ The degree is drifting doctoral; the law is not

Florida awarded 532 professional doctorates in nursing practice in 2023, against 522 master's in general nursing. NONPF's own trend data: DNP NP programmes 124 in 2014 to 254 in 2021; BSN-to-DNP graduates 934 in 2015 to 3,327 in 2021; entry to MSN NP programmes has levelled.

⚠⚠⚠ But NONPF is an association of faculties, and its 2025 commitment has no regulatory force. AANP and ANCC both still certify master's-prepared nurse practitioners, and only a state board of nursing can set the degree for licensure. Florida has not set one.

⚠ What to do with that: a master's still qualifies you, and the DNP is increasingly what programmes offer rather than what the law demands. Choose on the programme in front of you, not on a deadline that is not binding — and contrast it with the physician assistant route, where the master's requirement IS in Florida statute with a date.

⚠ A very wide base and a very narrow top

RungFL public institutionsCredentials (2023)
Registered nursing✅ 3910,372 — 5,037 associate, 4,774 bachelor's
Doctor of Nursing Practice⚠ 8538
⚠ Nurse anesthesia⚠⚠ 3⚠⚠ 55

⚠⚠ Roughly nineteen registered nursing credentials for every advanced practice one. The entry to nursing is among the most available things Florida teaches; the advanced rungs are among the least. Plan the graduate step deliberately and early, because you will probably have to move for it.

Necessary skills

  • Differential diagnosis — the skill nursing school does not teach and graduate school compresses into two courses, one of which Florida names in the autonomy statute.
  • Pharmacology at prescribing depth, likewise named in s. 464.0123.
  • Knowing the edge of your scope, which on this path is a legal boundary and not only a clinical one.
  • Practice management, if autonomy is the goal — billing, coding, liability coverage, contracting. Independence means running a business.
  • Years of registered nursing judgement. The statute wants 3,000 supervised hours for autonomy; the job wants considerably more.
  • Tolerance for an unsettled legal environment. Scope of practice is relitigated every session, and what you may do can change between one year and the next.

Advice

⚠⚠⚠ If you want to practise your specialty independently in Florida, read s. 464.0123 first. Autonomy is primary care. Psychiatry, acute care, oncology and the rest still need a protocol, and the 2024 bill that would have changed that for psychiatry died in subcommittee.

⚠⚠ Do not choose NP over PA on salary. They are within $3,580. Choose on whether you want independence in primary care or scope across all of medicine, because that is the actual difference and it is written into two statutes.

⚠ Get the RN and work. The 3,000 supervised hours the autonomy statute wants are hours you will accumulate anyway, and unlike the PA route you are licensed and paid the whole time. ⚠ If you stop after the BSN you still have a career.

⚠ Look hard at nurse anesthesia before dismissing it. $236,590 is not a rounding error. But three Florida public programmes, 55 graduates and 2,700 national openings a year mean you should expect to move and to compete.

And treat the DNP as a programme choice, not a deadline. The trend is real; the requirement is not, and nobody will refuse to certify you for holding a master's.

programs.note: The graduate step — 9 Florida public institutions. 8 award the DNP (UF 114, UNF 86, USF 83, FIU 81, UCF 69), 3 award nurse anesthesia at 55 credentials a year, and 2 award a named family nurse practitioner master's. ⚠ Read its degrees note on why the DNP is a trend rather than a requirement.

⚠⚠⚠ Always first, and the contrast in scale is the planning fact: 39 Florida public institutions award registered nursing degrees and produced 10,372 credentials in one year, against 538 at the doctoral level. ⚠ The RN years are also where the autonomy statute's 3,000 supervised clinical hours come from, so they are not a delay — they are the requirement.

⚠⚠ The alternative, decided on the statutes rather than the salary — the two medians are within $3,580. An APRN can practise autonomously in primary care; a PA cannot practise unsupervised at all, and a physician may supervise at most ten. ⚠ But a PA's scope reaches surgery and every specialty, and autonomous APRN practice reaches primary care only.

⚠ A common second credential rather than a route in, and the combination is unusually strong: a public health bachelor's alone is thin, and an MPH over a nursing licence is not. ⚠⚠ Population health, epidemiology and programme roles in county health departments are where the two meet.

⚠ The other graduate direction, and the more reachable one part-time: 24 Florida institutions with 20 state colleges carrying the upper-division coursework, against 9 for advanced practice nursing. ⚠⚠ Nurse executives sit in the medical and health services manager occupation at a $123,860 median — a real alternative for a nurse who wants off shift work without a clinical doctorate.

courses.reason: Anatomy and Physiology I — 20 institutions. The gate to every nursing programme in Florida, and the grade competitive admission usually turns on.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Two equivalent packagings: BSC2085 plus BSC2085L at 20 institutions, combined BSC2085C at 7. ⚠⚠ Also numbered APK2100C at some institutions — and BSC is what nursing prerequisite lists NAME, so take the BSC version unless your programme says otherwise.

courses.reason: Anatomy and Physiology I Laboratory — 19 institutions, the corequisite half.
Anatomy and Physiology II — 19 institutions. Cardiovascular, renal, endocrine and reproductive systems.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Also carried as the combined BSC2086C at 7 institutions.

courses.reason: Anatomy and Physiology II Laboratory — 19 institutions.
Microbiology — 16 institutions. Universal nursing prerequisite, and the basis for infection control and antibiotic prescribing later.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ MCB2010L, the laboratory, is carried at 15 and is separately required by most programmes.

courses.reason: Elementary Statistics — 39 institutions. Required for nursing admission and again for graduate work; evidence-based practice is the DNP's organising idea and it is statistical.
Introduction to Psychology — 33 institutions. A standard prerequisite, and behavioural health is a large share of primary care practice.
Developmental Psychology — 29 institutions. Commonly required, and directly relevant to paediatric and gerontological practice.
Human Nutrition — a standard nursing prerequisite and the foundation for chronic disease management, which is most of primary care.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Florida numbers nutrition several ways — HUN1201, HUN2201 and DIE prefixes. Check which your programme names.

courses.reason: Chemistry for Liberal Studies — carried very widely and carrying the (GE CORE) marker, so it satisfies the natural science area at every Florida public institution. ⚠ Check whether your nursing programme wants this or a majors chemistry sequence.
courses.variantNote: ⚠⚠ Nursing programmes differ sharply here: some accept a non-majors chemistry, some require CHM1045. Confirm before enrolling — it is a common and expensive mistake.

courses.reason: English Composition I — 39 institutions. Universal, and a nurse practitioner's documentation is a legal record and a billing document at once.
General Sociology — 29 institutions. Frequently required, and the social determinants framing is what primary care practice actually runs into.
Medical Terminology — 16 institutions. Cheap, universally useful, and usually assumed rather than required.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Florida numbers this twice: HSC1531 at 16 institutions and HSC2531 at 8.

sources.label: O*NET — Nurse Practitioners (29-1171.00)
sources.note: 320,400 employed (2024), growth much faster than average (7% or higher), 29,500 annual openings, median $132,300 (2025). Education 65% master's, 26% doctoral, 4% bachelor's. Tasks include diagnosing and treating acute, episodic or chronic illness independently or as part of a team, developing treatment plans, prescribing medications as legally authorized, and ordering or interpreting diagnostic tests.

Education 56% doctoral, 41% master's.

sources.label: O*NET — Nurse Midwives (29-1161.00)
sources.note: 8,600 employed, about 500 annual openings, median $134,040 (2025), growth much faster than average. Education 81% master's, 16% post-master's certificate. ⚠ The smallest of the three — and the only specialty Florida's autonomy statute actually unlocks beyond primary care.

Nursing practice, the DNP (51.3818): ⚠ 8 institutions, 538 credentials, 532 of them professional doctorates — UF 114, UNF 86, USF 83, FIU 81, UCF 69, FAU 40, FGCU 37, FSU 28. Nurse anesthesia (51.3804): 3 institutions, 55. Family nurse practitioner as a named master's (51.3805): 2 institutions, 127, with UWF awarding 95 of them.
